title: Testing pt2 pickle-guard behavior by swapping the sample-inputs record for a crafted payload
answers: how to test pt2 archive pickle rejection
write a test that a malicious pt2 payload is refused
test pytorch pt2 model with marker file payload
replace serialized_example_inputs record in pt2 test
body:
Use _replace_pt2_sample_inputs_record in tests/pytorch/test_pytorch_model_export.py. It saves a payload with torch.save into the archive's sample-inputs record, which torch.export.load unpickles with weights_only=False. Use a payload whose __reduce__ creates a marker file (_FileCreatingPayload), then assert that mlflow.pytorch.load_model and mlflow.pyfunc.load_model both raise with match on the record name and that the marker does not exist.
For the allowlist case, register the function with torch.serialization.safe_globals and assert the caller's allowlist is unchanged afterwards.
Gate these tests with skipif below torch 2.10. The helper finds the record by name suffix or the /sample_inputs/ path, since the name depends on the torch version.
applies: Tests of pt2 model loading with MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false in tests/pytorch.
says: Block arbitrary code execution when loading exported PyTorch models with pickle disabled.
Loading a suspicious PyTorch model archive should be rejected for security.
Untrusted sample inputs inside a PyTorch model execute code during loading.

Using a payload like _FileCreatingPayload, tests assert that mlflow.pytorch.load_model and mlflow.pyfunc.load_model raise matching the record name and that the marker file is not created.
